newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain labour minister sees 237,000 new jobs in '97.
newsitem.headline: Spain labour minister sees 237,000 new jobs in '97.

text.p: Spanish Labour Minister Javier Arenas said 237,000 new jobs may be created in 1997.

"New economic conditions can allow this objective to be achieved after two extraordinary pieces of data on inflation and interest rates which decisively affect economic growth in the coming year," Arenas said in an interview with the daily ABC published on Sunday.
Spanish inflation fell to 3.2 percent in November, compared to a 4.3 percent rise in 1995 and interest rates are at historic lows.
Arenas said the number of unemployed fell 150,000 in 1996, excluding December data.

In the third quarter, 3.51 million Spaniards were jobless with the unemployment rate at 21.90 percent, the highest in Europe, according to a survey compiled by the National Statistics Institute (INE).
The minister said the new jobs would not be created by the state although the government will try to provide the conditions for increased job creation.
Particularly, he said he was confident of labour reforms in 1997 which will contribute to creation of employment and encourage investment in Spain.
He said it was essential to introduce greater flexibility in the labour market by making it easier to fire workers.
